title: Mango chia protein pudding
summary: Blend it, split it between three jars, stir the chia in and leave it overnight. Thirty grams of protein and 8 g of fibre a pot, and the chia does all the thickening on its own.

time.note: Plus at least 2 hours in the fridge, ideally overnight.

nutrition_per_serving.note: One of three pots, assuming 0% Greek yogurt. Full-fat yogurt adds roughly 40 calories and 5 g of fat per pot. Carbs are total; quoted net of fibre the figure is about 23 g.

ingredients.note: Frozen works and is often sweeter than underripe fresh.
The only thickener here. Nothing else in the pot sets it.
Light, not the thick tinned kind, or the pots come out heavy.

steps: Blend the mango, coconut milk, Greek yogurt, honey and protein powder until smooth.
Divide the mixture between 3 pots or jars.

Stir 20 g of chia into each pot separately. Keep the chia out of the blender - blitzing it breaks the seeds up and they will not gel, and tipping the whole 60 g into one batch makes it clump before you can spread it.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, until thickened.
tips: Go back and stir each pot again after 15 to 20 minutes. Chia sinks fast, and left alone it sets as a dense layer at the bottom under a thin liquid top.
The nutrition assumes 0% Greek yogurt. Full-fat is nicer and costs about 40 calories and 5 g of fat a pot.
If it is too stiff by morning, loosen it with a splash of milk and stir.
These keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge, which is the point of making three at once.
health_notes: The 20 g of chia in each pot carries nearly all of the 8 g of fibre and about a third of the calories, so it is not a free thickener. The protein is split roughly evenly between the yogurt and the powder, which means it still lands near 20 g a pot without the scoop.

source.title: High Protein Mango Chia Seed Pudding | Try It Or Trash It @AdamHoadCoaching
source.adapted: Quantities are as given in the pinned comment on the video; the recipe originates with Adam Hoad (@AdamHoadCoaching) and this video is a cook-along of it. Nutrition checks out against the ingredient list at roughly 320 calories, 30 g protein, 10 g fat and 8 g fibre a pot, so the video's figures are recorded near enough as given. Its 23 g carbs is the same number quoted net of fibre; total carbs are about 30 g, which is what is recorded here.
